import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 486: Logarithmic density for sets avoiding modular subsets

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/486](https://www.erdosproblems.com/486)
-/

namespace Erdos486

/--
For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ choose some $X_n \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$.
Let $B = \{m \in \mathbb{N} : \forall n, m \not\equiv x \pmod{n} \text{ for all } x \in X_n\}$.
Must $B$ have a logarithmic density?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_486 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ X : (n : ℕ) → Set (ZMod n), ∃ d, {m : ℕ | ∀ n, (m : ZMod n) ∉ X n}.HasLogDensity d := by
  sorry

end Erdos486

findings.description: The set on line 34 tests avoidance for every modulus, whereas the source tests a modulus n only when n < m. This changes density existence, not merely finitely many elements. For an explicit positive-modulus example, put M_j = 2^(2^j) and S = {0} ∪ ⋃k [M_(2k), M_(2k+1)). Its normalized harmonic sums have subsequential limits 1/3 and 2/3. For each positive r outside S, set q_r = 2^(r+2) and X_(q_r) = {r}; set all other X_n, including X_0, empty. Let T = ⋃r {r + k*q_r : k ≥ 1}. The source's set is ℕ minus T and has natural density 1 − t, where T has natural density t ≤ 1/4: the remaining progression tails have uniformly bounded counting proportion at most ∑_(r>R) 1/q_r → 0. The Lean set is S minus T; its lower logarithmic density is at most 1/3 and its upper logarithmic density is at least 2/3 − t ≥ 5/12. Thus it has no logarithmic density. This defect is independent of allowing modulus zero.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/486 defines B using avoidance 'for all n in A with m > n'. Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory (1980), p. 114, likewise requires the residue inequalities only 'if b_u > a_i': https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the condition n < m in each residue-avoidance test and in the docstring. Fixing both reported defects gives the RHS: `∀ X : (n : ℕ) → Set (ZMod n), ∃ d, {m : ℕ | ∀ n, 0 < n → n < m → (m : ZMod n) ∉ X n}.HasLogDensity d`. This expression was type-checked in the scratch file.

findings.description: The modulus quantifiers include n = 0, and Mathlib defines ZMod 0 as ℤ. Consequently X 0 may impose an arbitrary, nonperiodic exclusion on the natural numbers. For any S : Set ℕ, choose X 0 = {z : ℤ | z.toNat ∉ S} and X (n+1) = ∅. The avoided set is exactly S. A sorry-free scratch proof establishes that the current RHS is equivalent to `∀ S : Set ℕ, ∃ d, S.HasLogDensity d`, which is false, for example for the alternating-block set in the other finding. Restoring only n < m does not repair this: the same construction then gives insert 0 S, with exactly the same logarithmic density behavior. Thus zero must independently be excluded from the tested moduli.
findings.source_evidence: Problem 486 concerns residue sets modulo positive natural-number moduli: https://www.erdosproblems.com/486. In the original formulation, Erdős (1980), p. 114, assigns a finite list of residues indexed by j = 1, …, t_i to each modulus a_i, not an arbitrary subset of ℤ. See https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf and the positive-integer setting of the cited Davenport–Erdős result, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1951-07.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict tested moduli to positive naturals, either by using ℕ+ throughout the modulus indexing or by adding `0 < n →` to the inner quantifier. The latter allows the existing total family X to remain unchanged, with X 0 unused. Also restore n < m as described in the other finding.

reformulations.difference: The source explicitly chooses a set A of active moduli and residue sets only for n ∈ A. The Lean statement omits A and instead chooses residue sets at every modulus. This aspect is legitimate, independently of the two missing domain restrictions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Extend a source family to all moduli by setting X_n = ∅ outside A. These additional indices impose no exclusions. Conversely, an everywhere-defined family is the special case A = ℕ (with only positive moduli tested). The corresponding universal density-existence statements, with the source's cutoff and positive moduli, are proved equivalent in `Review486.omit_index_set_iff`.

review.notes: The source currently marks the problem OPEN, agreeing with `research open`; `answer(sorry)` is correctly scoped and has type Prop. No separate status or answer-polarity issue was found. `HasLogDensity` uses the standard normalized harmonic sums. Including the term at zero contributes zero, and the denominator's default values at n = 0 and n = 1 affect only initial terms. The natural-versus-real cutoff and strict-versus-inclusive summation endpoint give equivalent limits. Scratch proofs in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish the modulus-zero reductions, the index-set reformulation, and the harmonic normalization/zero-term identities; the final compile succeeds, and the inspected proof dependencies contain no sorryAx. The positive-modulus counterexample for the missing cutoff is an informal proof recorded in /workspace/review/cutoff-counterexample.md, not a claimed Lean proof. The reviewed file was not modified.
